title: PalliDrone - Scientific evaluation of the effectiveness and added value of drone-based medication delivery in palliative care
summary:
The core idea of palliative medicine is to provide support and comprehensive care for people with incurable, life-threatening illnesses. If there is no prospect of a cure, those affected and their relatives should be enveloped and protected as if by a cloak (Latin pallium = cloak). But how can this difficult and complex task be achieved against the backdrop of demographic developments and the increasing shortage of specialists, especially in rural regions of Germany? 

Compared to urban areas, rural regions often face the problem of a lower density of medical facilities and specialist staff. This can lead to limited access to palliative care and places an additional burden on both patients and their families. The geographical distribution of rural areas can make access to palliative services and professionals even more difficult. 
Despite these challenges, there are also positive developments and initiatives aimed at improving palliative care in rural areas. In a previous feasibility study ("ADApp"), it was shown that contactless delivery of medicines in rural areas can be realized through a pharmacy app in combination with drone logistics. 
Based on these findings and preliminary investigations, the aim of the "PalliDrohne" study is to implement drone-based medication delivery in a palliative care context. The aim is to investigate whether this form of care offers added value for palliative patients, their caregiving relatives and hospice and SAPV staff. 

In the form of a so-called "living lab", the requirements, challenges and opportunities will be identified under real-life conditions in order to characterizes the necessities for implementation.
The focus is not only on the time to delivery of medicines, but also on the perception of quality of life and the relief of nursing staff and caregiving relatives that can be provided by drone-based medicine delivery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Palliative care patients in inpatient and outpatient care who are cared for by their family members or SAPV staff are included. Further criteria for inclusion are a minimum age of 18 years and sufficient written and spoken German language skills. In addition, it is stipulated that at least two deliveries per included patient must be made by courier or drone. Patients who are unable to give consent are also included.
Exclusion criteria:
No explicit exclusion criteria are defined. Exclusion occurs if the inclusion criteria do not apply.
